title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does ModExp handle all edge case inputs deterministically?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Abstract interpretation analysis of ModExp precompile edge case handling reveals critical state-space anomalies in the input domain. The property requires deterministic gas cost computation and result consistency across all edge cases. Analysis identifies multiple abstract domains where overflow, division-by-zero, and cross-client non-determinism can occur.

context_resolution.location: Execution Layer Precompiled Contract at address 0x05
context_resolution.note: Prysm is a consensus layer client. ModExp precompile is implemented in execution layer clients (e.g., Geth, Nethermind, Besu, Erigon). This analysis is performed at the specification level and applies to all execution clients that Prysm validators interact with.

abstract_domain.safety_constraint: Must not cause integer overflow in downstream computations
Must not cause overflow in 16*(exponent_length-32) computation
Must not cause integer overflow in ceil(modulus_length/8)^2

cases.overflow_risk: words^2 can overflow if max_length is very large

cases.note: bit_length implementation variance is a consensus risk

abstract_transformations.anomaly: none for division, but note rounding semantics must be consistent
CRITICAL - Integer overflow: words^2 overflows when words > sqrt(2^256-1) ≈ 2^128. For max_length > 8 * 2^128, overflow occurs.
abstract_transformations.exploitability: Attacker provides max_length near 2^256-1, causing words ≈ 2^253, words^2 overflows to small value, gas_cost wraps to minimal.

abstract_transformations.anomaly: CRITICAL - Integer overflow: 16 * (exponent_length - 32) overflows when exponent_length > (2^256-1)/16 + 32 ≈ 2^252.
abstract_transformations.exploitability: Attacker provides exponent_length near 2^256-1, causing 16*(exponent_length-32) to overflow, iteration_count wraps to small value.

abstract_transformations.anomaly: CRITICAL - Integer overflow: Even if complexity and iterations individually fit in uint256, their product can overflow. E.g., complexity=2^128, iterations=2^128 => product=2^256 (wraps to 0).
abstract_transformations.exploitability: Attacker balances large max_length and large exponent_length to maximize product overflow.
abstract_transformations.mitigation_required: Overflow-checked multiplication or gas cap enforcement before computation

abstract_transformations.anomaly: If product overflows to small value, gas = max(500, small_value) = 500, but actual computational cost is enormous. DoS vector.
abstract_transformations.consensus_impact: If clients differ in overflow handling (panic vs wrap vs saturate), gas costs diverge => consensus failure.

abstract_state.post: words ∈ [2^128, 2^253], words^2 overflows => complexity wraps to small value or panics

state_anomalies_found.impact: Gas underpricing by factor of up to 2^256 / actual_cost. Network-wide DoS if overflow wraps. Consensus failure if clients differ (panic vs wrap).
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: HIGH - Attacker controls base_length and modulus_length via contract calldata.

counterexample.actual_behavior_if_overflow: words = 2^237, words^2 overflows, complexity wraps to small value, gas ≈ 500

state_anomalies_found.impact: Gas underpricing. Large exponent becomes nearly free. DoS attack vector.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: HIGH - Attacker controls exponent_length via contract calldata.

counterexample.actual_behavior_if_overflow: iterations wraps to small value, gas ≈ 500

abstract_state.post: product = complexity * iterations overflows => gas wraps to small value

state_anomalies_found.impact: Catastrophic gas underpricing. Extremely expensive computation for 500 gas.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: CRITICAL - Attacker can balance max_length and exponent_length to maximize product while staying under individual overflow thresholds.

state_anomalies_found.type: Division by Zero / Edge Case Non-determinism
state_anomalies_found.trigger_condition: exponent_length <= 32 AND all exponent bytes are 0x00

abstract_state.post: iteration_count must equal exactly 1 per spec

state_anomalies_found.impact: If iteration_count is computed as bit_length(0) - 1 = -1 (or 0 in unsigned), gas formula fails. Cross-client inconsistency if some use bit_length(0)=0 and others use bit_length(0)=1.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: MEDIUM - Easy to trigger, but impact depends on implementation details.

state_anomalies_found.impact: 3.125x gas cost jump from max_length=32 to max_length=33. If clients use different comparison operators (< vs <=), consensus divergence.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: MEDIUM - Attacker targets boundary to expose client implementation differences.

state_anomalies_found.impact: Off-by-one in iteration_count across clients => consensus failure.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: HIGH - Attacker probes power-of-2 exponent boundaries.

counterexample.gas_divergence: Different gas costs for identical inputs

state_anomalies_found.impact: Spec ambiguity: Does max_length=0 use small path (complexity=16) or is it undefined? Different clients may implement differently.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: MEDIUM - Zero-length operands are edge cases that may not be tested cross-client.

counterexample.client_B: max_length = 0 => special case early return or error
counterexample.consensus_risk: Different gas costs or execution results

abstract_state.order_of_operations: If implementation allocates buffers before computing gas, OOM occurs

state_anomalies_found.impact: Node crash before gas deduction. DoS with minimal gas expenditure.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: CRITICAL - Attacker can crash validator nodes with low-gas transactions.

counterexample.expected_behavior: Compute gas cost first, revert with out-of-gas
counterexample.vulnerable_behavior: Allocate 1GB buffer, OOM crash before gas check

state_anomalies_found.impact: If different clients use different ceiling implementations with rounding errors, words differs by 1 => complexity differs significantly.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: MEDIUM - Rounding errors at odd max_length values.

state_anomalies_found.type: Input Length vs Data Length Mismatch
state_anomalies_found.location: Reading base, exponent, modulus from calldata

abstract_state.post: Implementation reads past end of calldata

state_anomalies_found.impact: Different clients may handle out-of-bounds reads differently: zero-padding vs error vs garbage. Consensus divergence.
state_anomalies_found.exploitability: HIGH - Attacker declares large lengths but provides minimal calldata.

reachability_analysis.attacker_control: Full control over calldata (base_length, exponent_length, modulus_length, and data bytes)
exploitation_path: Contract calls ModExp with crafted edge case inputs
Gas underpricing or cross-client divergence achieved
Network-wide impact: DoS via resource exhaustion or consensus failure

cross_client_determinism_requirements: All clients must use identical overflow handling: checked arithmetic with panic/revert on overflow (NOT wrapping)
All clients must use identical bit_length definition and implementation
All clients must use identical ceiling division implementation
All clients must use identical boundary condition comparisons (<=32 vs <32)
All clients must handle zero-length inputs identically
All clients must validate calldata bounds identically (zero-pad vs error)
All clients must compute gas BEFORE allocating memory
All clients must use identical exponent=0 special case handling
recommended_verification_approach: Differential fuzzing: Generate random edge case inputs, execute on all clients, compare gas costs and results
Boundary value testing: Test all identified critical boundaries (0, 1, 32, 33, 2^8, 2^64, 2^128, 2^252, 2^256-1)
Overflow testing: Craft inputs designed to overflow each intermediate computation
Cross-client test suite: Canonical test vectors with expected gas costs
Formal verification: Prove overflow-freedom and determinism using SMT solvers
